text: Or do you not know, brothers — I am speaking to people who know the law — that the law has authority over a person only as long as that person lives?
A married woman is bound by law to her husband while he lives, but if her husband dies, she is released from the law that bound her to him.

So then, if she gives herself to another man while her husband is alive, she is called an adulteress. But if her husband dies, she is free from that law, and she is no adulteress if she marries another man.

Therefore, my brothers, you also were put to death with regard to the law through the body of Christ, so that you might belong to another — to him who was raised from the dead — in order that we might bear fruit for God.

versions.text: In the same way, my brothers, you also were put to death with regard to the law through the body of Christ, so that you might belong to another — to him who was raised from the dead — in order that we might bear fruit for God.
versions.explanation: Ὥστε is an inferential conjunction ("therefore," "so then"), drawing a conclusion from the marriage illustration. "In the same way" makes it a comparison rather than a conclusion, which weakens Paul's argument.

text: For when we were in the flesh, the sinful passions aroused by the law were at work in our members, bearing fruit for death.
But now we have been released from the law, having died to what once held us captive, so that we serve in the new way of the Spirit and not in the old way of the written code.
What shall we say, then? Is the law sin? By no means! Yet I would not have known sin except through the law. I would not have known what coveting is if the law had not said, "You shall not covet."
But sin seized its opportunity through the commandment and produced in me every kind of coveting. For apart from the law, sin is dead.
Once I was alive apart from the law; but when the commandment came, sin sprang to life
and I died. So the very commandment that was meant to bring life turned out to bring death to me.
For sin seized its opportunity through the commandment, deceived me, and through it put me to death.
So then, the law is holy, and the commandment is holy, righteous, and good.

Did that which is good, then, become death to me? By no means! It was sin — so that sin might be exposed as sin, working death in me through what is good; so that through the commandment sin might be shown to be utterly sinful.
For we know that the law is spiritual; but I am of the flesh, sold as a slave to sin.

versions.text: We know that the law is spiritual; but I am of the flesh, sold as a slave to sin.
versions.explanation: The explanatory γάρ links this verse to the preceding argument and is untranslated; adding "For" preserves the logical connection and reads naturally aloud.

text: For I do not understand what I do. What I want to do, I do not do; instead, I do what I hate.
And if I do what I do not want to do, I agree that the law is good.
So it is no longer I myself who do it, but the sin that lives in me.
For I know that nothing good lives in me — that is, in my flesh. The will is there, but the ability to do what is good is not.
For I do not do the good I want to do; instead, I do the evil I do not want to do.
And if I do what I do not want to do, then it is no longer I who do it, but the sin that lives in me.
So I find this law at work: when I want to do good, evil lies close at hand.
For in my inner self I delight in God's law,
but I see another law in my members, waging war against the law of my mind and making me a prisoner of the law of sin that dwells in my members.

versions.text: but I see another law at work in my members, waging war against the law of my mind and taking me captive to the law of sin that is at work in my members.
versions.explanation: The phrase "at work in my members" is repeated twice in one sentence, which is clumsy for oral reading, and "at work" is not in the Greek (the participle is simply ὄντι, "being/that is").

text: What a wretched man I am! Who will rescue me from this body of death?
Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord! So then, I myself serve the law of God with my mind, but with my flesh the law of sin.
